source: YASKAWA AC Drive – A1000 Technical Manual, doc SIEP C710616 41H, Appendix C (MEMOBUS/Modbus Communications), downloaded directly from yaskawa.com. Every entry in this file that lacks an explicit "verified": false marker was checked word-for-word against that PDF (page numbers cited per section) while correcting src/a1000_modbus_old.json. See a1000_modbus_corrections.md for the full list of what changed and why.
notes: Factory default slave address: 1F (hex) = 31 (dec), set via parameter H5-01. Range is 0-FF; 0 disables responses (broadcast-only).
Broadcast address 00 is write-only; no response is returned. Broadcast may only target register 0001H or 0002H (MEMOBUS/Modbus error 02H otherwise).

H5-03 (Communication Parity Selection) controls PARITY ONLY: 0=None (default), 1=Even, 2=Odd. It does NOT select stop bits directly. The A1000 manual does not document a separate stop-bit parameter; the firmware's SERIAL_8N2 (8 data bits, no parity, 2 stop bits) matches H5-03=0 under the standard Modbus RTU convention of 2 stop bits when no parity is used. Confirm this against your specific drive if you rely on it.
Register addresses: use the Yaskawa MEMOBUS register number directly as the PDU address. No offset is applied.

Frequency reference and most frequency/speed monitor values are in units of 0.01 Hz BY DEFAULT (parameter o1-03 = 0). o1-03 can select 0.01% or r/min instead (o1-03 = 1 or 2) or gets forced to 1 (%) automatically when A1-02 (Control Method) = 6 or 7. Do not assume 0.01 Hz unconditionally.
The output voltage monitor at register 0025H has its own separate unit selector, H5-10 (0 = 0.1 V default, 1 = 1 V) — independent of o1-03.
All multi-byte values in the PDU are big-endian (high byte first), per standard Modbus RTU.

CRC is CRC-16/IBM (polynomial 0x8005 reflected = 0xA001), initialised to 0xFFFF, appended little-endian (low byte first on wire). Verified against every example message in this file by direct computation.
The A1000 uses standard Modbus RTU framing. There is no 0x4000 address offset on the A1000; that scheme applies to some older Yaskawa drives (e.g. G7/P7) only.

b1-01 must be set to 2 (Modbus) for frequency reference commands to take effect. b1-02 must be set to 2 (Modbus) for run/stop/direction commands to take effect. Confirmed verbatim in Technical Manual Table C.2 (p.710).

H5-12 (Run Command Method Selection, default 0) controls what command-register bits 0-1 mean: default (0) = independent FWD/Stop and REV/Stop bits (bit0 alone runs forward, bit1 alone runs reverse) — this is what this project's firmware assumes. Setting 1 changes bit0 to a generic Run/Stop and bit1 to a Forward/Reverse direction selector instead. If bit-0/bit-1 behavior looks wrong on your drive, check H5-12 first.

H5-01.name: Drive Slave Address
H5-01.note: 0 = broadcast-only, drive never responds. Power-cycle to apply.

H5-03.name: Communication Parity Selection
H5-03.note: Parity only. See notes[] above re: stop bits. Power-cycle to apply.

map.0: Disabled — no CE detection, drive continues
map.1: Enabled — CE fault triggered per H5-09

H5-06.name: Drive Transmit Wait Time
H5-06.note: Delay after receiving a request before the drive starts responding. Power-cycle to apply.

map.1: RTS controlled (switches while sending) — RS-485 or multi-drop RS-422

H5-09.name: Communications Fault Detection Time
H5-09.description: How long comms must be lost before a CE fault triggers (when H5-05 = 1).

H5-10.name: Unit Selection for MEMOBUS/Modbus Register 0025H
H5-10.description: Governs ONLY the output voltage reference monitor at register 0025H.

H5-11.name: Communications Enter Function Selection
H5-11.description: Whether/when parameter writes take effect relative to the Enter command (registers 0900H/0910H). See C.10 Enter Command.

map.0: FWD/Stop, REV/Stop — command register bit0 alone runs forward, bit1 alone runs reverse (default; matches this project's firmware)
map.1: Run/Stop, FWD/REV — bit0 is generic run/stop, bit1 selects direction

required_parameter_setup.description: These parameters must be set on the A1000 before Modbus control is active. Confirmed verbatim in Technical Manual Table C.2 (p.710).

b1-01.verification_note: Command requirement (value=2) confirmed in Table C.2; the specific parameter-space register address 0x0180 was carried over from the prior version of this file and not independently re-confirmed against the manual's parameter address table in this pass.

03.name: Read Holding Registers
03.description: Read one or more 16-bit holding registers. Response: [slave][03][byte_count][data HI][data LO]...[CRC_LO][CRC_HI]. Confirmed supported — used throughout example_messages and by this project's real-hardware testing.

06.name: Write Single Register
06.description: Write a single 16-bit holding register. Drive echoes the request unchanged on success. Confirmed supported by direct testing against real A1000 hardware this session (run/reverse/stop/freq commands).

08.name: Loopback Test
08.description: Diagnostics loopback. Sub-function 0x0000 echoes the data word back unchanged. Confirmed supported (manual p.733 references it explicitly).

10.name: Write Multiple Registers (FC 16)
10.description: Write multiple consecutive 16-bit holding registers in one message. Confirmed supported (manual p.733).

function_codes.note: The manual's error-01H description (p.733) names only 03H, 08H, and 10H as valid function codes, but 06H is demonstrably supported (see above) — that phrasing is likely incomplete rather than exhaustive. Function codes 01 and 02 (coil/discrete input reads) from the prior version of this file were removed: they're generic Modbus definitions with no evidence the A1000 implements them, and the manual's own function-code list doesn't mention them.

command_data.description: MEMOBUS register range 0000H-001FH. Read/write. Source: Technical Manual Table C.5 "Command Register Data", p.716-717.

0001.name: Operation Commands and Multi-Function Inputs

0.name: Forward Run / Run
0.description: H5-12=0 (default): Forward Run Command (0=Stop, 1=Forward Run). H5-12=1: generic Run Command (0=Stop, 1=Run).

1.name: Reverse Run / Direction
1.description: H5-12=0 (default): Reverse Run Command (0=Stop, 1=Reverse Run). H5-12=1: Forward/Reverse select (0=Forward, 1=Reverse).

3.name: Fault Reset
3.description: Rising edge resets an active fault; clear back to 0 after.

4.name: Multi-Function Input 1
4.description: Generic, user-configurable input. Acts as ComRef when H1-01 = 40 (Forward/Stop). When the bit mapped to ComCtrl is on, MEMOBUS/Modbus commands take control (unless a comm option card is connected, which takes priority).

5.name: Multi-Function Input 2
5.description: Generic, user-configurable input. Acts as ComCtrl when H1-02 = 41 (Reverse/Stop).

0001.correction_note: The prior version of this file assigned fixed meanings to bits 4-13 (Multi-step Ref, Jog, Accel/Decel Select, Baseblock, Torque Reference, Speed/Torque Sel, Emergency Stop, KEB, Drive Enable). Those are fabricated — bits 4-11 are generic Multi-Function Inputs (whatever function you assign via H1-01..H1-08), and bits 12-13 are Reserved, not KEB/Drive Enable.

0003.name: Output voltage gain / bias
0003.correction_note: Prior version of this file mislabeled this register as 'PID Feedback Reference'.

0004.name: Torque Reference / Torque Limit
0004.note: Usable only if Torque Control is enabled.

0005.name: Torque Compensation
0005.note: Usable only if Torque Control is enabled.

12.name: Enable Terminal S5 Input for Broadcast Data

13.name: Enable Terminal S6 Input for Broadcast Data

14.name: Enable Terminal S7 Input for Broadcast Data

15.name: Enable Terminal S8 Input for Broadcast Data

001B.name: Analog Monitor Option AO-A3 Analog Output 1

001C.name: Analog Monitor Option AO-A3 Analog Output 2

monitor_data.description: Read-only unless noted. Source: Technical Manual Table C.5 continuation "Monitor Data" and Table C.6/C.7, p.717-719, 729-731. This entirely replaces the prior version's 'status_registers'/'monitor_registers' sections, which had register 0021H, 0022H, 0023H, 0025H and others mismatched or misassigned — most importantly 0025H, which the prior file called 'Output Frequency' but is actually Output Voltage Reference (confirmed both in this table and in parameter H5-10's own description). Real Output Frequency is 0024H.

0020.name: Drive Status 1
0020.correction_note: Only bit 0 matched the prior version of this file. Every other bit was wrong there — most importantly, this project's firmware currently reads bit 2 expecting 'Reverse Running'; the real bit 2 is Drive Ready (nearly always 1 when healthy), and real 'During Reverse' is bit 1.

0021.name: Fault Contents 1
0021.type: 16-bit bitmask of fault CATEGORIES, NOT a single enumerated fault code

4.name: Dynamic Braking Transistor Fault (rr), Braking Resistor Overheat (rH)

9.name: Motor Overload (oL1), Overtorque Detection 1/2 (oL3/oL4), Undertorque Detection 1/2 (UL3/UL4)

10.name: PG Disconnected (PGo), PG Hardware Fault (PGoH), Overspeed (oS), Speed Deviation (dEv)

12.name: DC Bus Undervoltage (Uv1), Control Power Supply Voltage Fault (Uv2), Undervoltage 3 (Uv3)

13.name: Output Phase Loss (LF), Input Phase Loss (PF)

14.name: MEMOBUS/Modbus Communication Error (CE), Option Communication Error (bUS)

0021.correction_note: The prior version of this file treated 0021H as a simple 0x00-0x3A enumerated fault code with a switch/case-style name table (this project's vfd_fault_name() in main.cpp mirrors that assumption). It is not — see fault_and_alarm_codes below for the actual single-value fault code registers.

0022.name: Data Link Status

5.name: Writing to EEPROM
5.description: 0 = write into EEPROM, 1 = write in RAM only. Enabled only when H5-17 = 1.

0022.correction_note: Prior version of this file called this register 'Alarm Code'. It is not — see fault_and_alarm_codes below for the real alarm/minor-fault registers.

0023.name: Frequency Reference
0023.note: Value <1> — see manual footnote on units (o1-03 dependent).
0023.correction_note: Prior version of this file called this register 'Drive Status 2' with a fabricated bitmask. The real Drive Status 2 bitmask is at 002CH (see below).

0024.name: Output Frequency
0024.note: Value <1> — see manual footnote on units (o1-03 dependent).
0024.correction_note: This is the register this project's firmware should be reading for output frequency; it currently reads 0025H instead.

0025.name: Output Voltage Reference
0025.correction_note: Prior version of this file — and this project's firmware — treat 0025H as Output Frequency. It is Output Voltage Reference.

0026.name: Output Current
0026.note: Units vary by drive model/rating: 0.01 A on smaller models, 0.1 A on mid-range, 1 A on the largest (4A0930, 4A1200).

0028.name: Torque Reference
0028.correction_note: Prior version of this file called this register 'DC Bus Voltage'. Real DC Bus Voltage is 0031H.

0.name: Output Short Circuit or IGBT Fault (SC)

fault_and_alarm_codes.description: The A1000 exposes fault/alarm information through THREE distinct MEMOBUS/Modbus mechanisms, each with its own numbering — they are not interchangeable. The prior version of this file conflated them into a single fault_codes table keyed to register 0021H, which is wrong on two counts: 0021H is a bitmask (see monitor_data above), and none of these three real numbering schemes matches the numbers that table used.

fault_contents_1_bitmask.note: See monitor_data.registers.0021 above for the full bit table.

minor_fault_code.source: Technical Manual Table C.7 "Alarm Register 007FH Contents", p.731.

codes.001B: Motor Switch command input during run (rUn)
codes.0043: Soft Charge Bypass Relay Maintenance Time (LT-3)

minor_fault_code.note: Table trimmed to the codes most relevant to this project (option-card-specific and MECHATROLINK-specific codes omitted). Full table in the Technical Manual if needed.

current_fault_code.source: Technical Manual Table C.6 "Fault Trace / History Register Contents", p.729-730.

codes.0011: External Fault at Input Terminal S3 (EF3)
codes.0012: External Fault at Input Terminal S4 (EF4)
codes.0013: External Fault at Input Terminal S5 (EF5)
codes.0014: External Fault at Input Terminal S6 (EF6)
codes.0015: External Fault at Input Terminal S7 (EF7)
codes.0016: External Fault at Input Terminal S8 (EF8)

current_fault_code.note: Table trimmed to the codes most relevant to this project (oFx option-card sub-codes, dv/CPF sub-codes, and MECHATROLINK-specific codes omitted — see Technical Manual Table C.6 for the full ~90-entry list, including CPF00-CPF45 hardware faults at 0083H-009FH+). Note this table's values for oC (0007H), ov (0008H), etc. do NOT match the numbers this project's firmware currently expects (0x01, 0x02, ...) — see a1000_modbus_corrections.md.
current_fault_code.recommended_fix: Have the firmware read register 0080H (not 0021H) for a decodable single fault value, and rebuild the name-lookup table against these codes.

exception_responses.description: If the drive cannot process a request it responds with the function code OR'd with 0x80, followed by a drive-specific exception code and CRC. Source: Technical Manual C.11 Communication Errors, p.733. These codes are A1000-specific, not the generic Modbus exception code list.

01.name: Function Code Error
01.description: A function code other than 03H, 08H, or 10H was used (06H also confirmed supported in practice — see function_codes note).

02.name: Register Number Error
02.description: A register number in the command doesn't exist, or a broadcast message used a register other than 0001H/0002H.

03.name: Bit Count Error
03.description: Read/write data exceeds 16 bits, or a write message's byte count doesn't match its data.

21.name: Data Setting Error
21.description: Control data or parameter write data is outside the allowable range, or a contradictory parameter setting was attempted.

22.name: Write Mode Error
22.description: Wrote a parameter that can't change during Run, wrote to read-only data, or (during a CPF06 EEPROM error) wrote to a parameter other than A1-00..A1-05/E1-03/o2-04.

23.name: DC Bus Undervoltage Write Error
23.description: Attempted to write a parameter that can't be written during an undervoltage condition.

24.name: Write Error During Parameter Process
24.description: Wrote to the drive while it was still processing previous parameter data.

25.name: Writing into EEPROM Disabled
25.description: Attempted an EEPROM write via Modbus while EEPROM writes are disabled. Drive continues operating; only the write is rejected.

exception_responses.correction_note: Prior version of this file used the generic standard-Modbus exception code list (01=Illegal Function, 02=Illegal Data Address, 03=Illegal Data Value, 04=Slave Device Failure, 05=Acknowledge, 06=Slave Device Busy). Codes 01-03 happen to be conceptually similar to the real A1000-specific codes above (hence likely why they were assumed), but 04-06 don't exist on the A1000, and the real drive additionally defines 21H-25H, which the prior version omitted entirely.

example_messages.description: Complete raw Modbus RTU byte sequences. Format: [slave][FC][...data...][CRC_LO][CRC_HI]. Every CRC below was independently recomputed and verified correct (CRC-16/Modbus, poly 0xA001, init 0xFFFF) — see a1000_modbus_corrections.md for the verification method. Carried over unchanged from the prior version of this file.

read_status_register.response_note: XX XX = 16-bit status word (Drive Status 1 — see monitor_data.registers.0020), high byte first.

read_status_and_fault_bitmask.description: Read Drive Status 1 (0x0020) and Fault Contents 1 bitmask (0x0021) in one request from slave 01
read_status_and_fault_bitmask.response_note: XX XX = status word, YY YY = fault bitmask (not a simple code — see fault_and_alarm_codes).

read_output_frequency.description: Read actual output frequency from slave 01 — corrected to the real Output Frequency register, 0x0024 (was 0x0025 in the prior version of this file, which is actually Output Voltage Reference).

read_multiple_monitors.description: Read 6 monitor registers starting at 0x0023: Frequency Reference, Output Frequency, Output Voltage Reference, Output Current, Output Power, Torque Reference — from slave 01. Corrected start address (was 0x0025 in the prior version, which produced a different 6-register window not aligned to those six monitors).

set_frequency_60hz.description: Set frequency reference to 60.00 Hz (6000 = 0x1770) on slave 01 — at o1-03 default units
set_frequency_60hz.response_note: FC 06 success: drive echoes the full request unchanged.

run_forward.description: Run forward (command word bit 0 = 1) on slave 01. Requires H5-12 = 0 (default).

run_reverse.description: Run reverse (command word bit 1 = 1, bit 0 must be 0) on slave 01. Requires H5-12 = 0 (default).

stop.description: Stop (command word all zeros) on slave 01

fault_reset.description: Reset active fault on slave 01. Step 1: set bit 3 (rising edge). Step 2: clear to 0.
fault_reset.note: Wait at least 50 ms between step 1 and step 2.

run_forward_and_set_freq_together.description: Write command word (run forward) and frequency reference (60.00 Hz) in one FC 10 transaction on slave 01
run_forward_and_set_freq_together.response_note: FC 10 success response echoes start address (00 01) and register count (00 02).

loopback_test.description: FC 08 loopback diagnostic (sub-function 0x0000) to slave 01. Drive echoes the two data bytes unchanged.

exception_example.description: Example exception response: slave 01, FC 03 request failed with A1000 exception 02H (Register Number Error)

parameter_registers.verification_note: This section (drive parameter addresses like A1-02, C1-01, d1-01, E1-04, H5-01, etc., accessed via the parameter address space rather than the command/monitor registers above) was carried over from the prior version of a1000_modbus.json largely as-is. Only d1-01 (0x0280) and the H5-0x parameters (moved into communication_parameters above, with corrected addresses 0x0320-0x0326) were independently re-confirmed against the Technical Manual in this pass. Cross-check any other entry here against your manual before relying on it, especially before scripting parameter writes.

0280.name: Frequency Reference 1
0280.verification_note: Confirmed at this address in Technical Manual p.578.

scaling_summary.note: Generic unit conventions, not tied to a single register. Cross-check against the specific register/parameter in monitor_data or parameter_registers above.

dc_bus_voltage.verification_note: Confirmed: register 0031H, '1 Vdc units', Technical Manual p.719.
